  slope of every thread that sum is the weave's own operation: every thread, every slope, none chosen.
- It diverges, because each thread's fillings pile up just below its own volume. Stanford and Yan (arXiv 2510.19920,
  2025) propose to cancel such pile-ups with the cusped manifold itself, as a counterterm.

**The order.**
- The rule (`W125_RULE.md`, c251c5e2f) was committed and pushed before the script. It disclosed Neumann–Zagier seen on
  20 fillings and the literature read.
- The script (eba4ae5f2) was committed after crash checks on inputs outside the census. It was run once, in about two
  minutes on four workers, and its output (d9ac5a3e1) was committed unread, then read once.

**The result (COMPUTED; K0–K3 held; K4 failed as worded).**
- **K0.** 641 730 fillings in all, 15 258 to 15 290 per thread; 641 374 certified.
  - Every thread's volume equals W122's exactly.
  - The counts are within 0.14% of (3/π)·16 000.
  - No slope with Q > 60 fails; the largest Q among the 356 uncertified slopes is 23.3.
  - The least certified volume is the Weeks manifold's, 0.9427073628, at b+-LR's slope (3, 5).
- **K1.** Q(V_b − V)/π² is within 0.0047 of 1 for every certified filling with Q ≥ 400, on every thread.
- **K2.** Q·ℓ/2π is within 0.0094 of 1 on the same fillings.
- **K3,** from each thread's cusp shape alone:
  - (a) the finite part of the slope count, 2F(0.002) − F(0.004), is within 0.0010 of 1 on every thread;
  - (b) the log coefficient's ratio is 1.0030 on every thread, the predicted O(ε) shift (ε/((3/π) log 2) = 0.0030);
  - (c) Stanford and Yan's (3.30) holds to 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁵ on every thread. The full lattice's corrections stop at O(ε),
    since its Epstein function vanishes at the negative integers, so the Richardson value is exact.
- **K4 FAILED as worded.**
  - At s = ½ and 1 every thread's remainder moved by at most 0.0075 and 0.036 between ε = 0.004 and 0.002.
  - At s = 2 four threads exceeded the rule's 0.5: b+-LLRLR and b+-LRLRR by 0.87, and b+-LLLRLR and b+-LRLRRR by 1.45.
    The next largest was 0.38.
  - Over the same step the bare towers moved by 242 to 257.
- **K5 (read-out; this scheme).**
  - The uncertified slopes number 4 to 14 per thread. b++LR has 10, the number of the figure-eight knot's exceptional
    slopes.
  - The second-order coefficient's median is between −0.034 and 0.038 on every thread.
  - The renormalized ensemble Z_ren(s) is −117.0, −31.1, −1.28 and +0.175 at s = ½, 1, 2 and 4. The Richardson values
    are −117.5, −31.0, −1.18 and +0.183. The cusped ensemble Σ_b e^{−s·V_b} is 6.61, 1.30, 0.080 and 0.00073.
  - The largest single term is the tick's tower, b++LR, at s = ½, 1 and 2 (6%, 12% and 43% of Z_ren), and its sister's,
    b+-LR, at s = 4 (48%).
  - The Weeks manifold's own term is −0.5%, −1.3%, −12% and +13% of Z_ren.

**What failed, and the checks after the read-out (post hoc, labelled).**
1. **K4's tolerance was wrong by design.**
   - It counted only the far tail's O(Q⁻²) term. But the cut also acts on the slopes with small Q, where the
     Neumann–Zagier subtraction e^{sπ²/Q} is large: e^{6.6} at Q = 3 and s = 2. Those are finitely many finite terms,
     and the cut moves them linearly in ε.
   - The run's own JSON shows this (`the_quantum_weave_posthoc.py`; no new filling).
     - The successive differences of the remainder, as ε halves from 0.016 to 0.002, have ratios 1.81 to 2.18 wherever
       the last exceeds 0.01. A divergence would give ratios of 1 or less.
     - All of the last drift comes from slopes with Q ≤ 100. The part from Q > 100 is at most 0.13 anywhere: at s = 4,
       where the whole drift is 1068. At s ≤ 2 it is below 0.003.
     - The Richardson limits are finite: −240.2 on b+-LLLRLR at s = 2, for instance.
   - So the remainder converges, and the divergence is exactly the universal form. This holds post hoc, not as the
     rule worded it.
2. **The count per universe** (post hoc, SnapPy's self-isometries of each thread).
   - The run summed (thread, slope) pairs. A sum over distinct oriented universes would divide a thread's count by any
     orientation-preserving symmetry's action on its slopes.
   - On all 42 threads every orientation-preserving self-isometry acts on the cusp as ±1, so it fixes every slope.
     Distinct slopes on one thread give distinct oriented universes, and the coefficient 3/π holds per universe.
   - Mirror words give mirror spaces. Oriented gravity counts these separately, since their Chern–Simons invariants
     differ in sign.
   - Coincidences between threads are not checked. The Meyerhoff manifold fills both ±LR; such coincidences change
     finite parts only, unless infinitely many coincide.

**What this does (READING; the rule's fixed outcomes, with K4 held only post hoc, so labelled).**
1. **No bare ground state.** The sum over every closed universe the record's threads fill diverges at every coupling,
   because its slope count alone grows like (3/π)X (K0, K3). W122's "ground state" is a statement about single closed
   universes, not about the quantum sum.
2. **The threads are the counterterms.** At tree level each thread's tower diverges as
   e^{−s·V_b}·(3/(πε) + 3πs·log(1/ε)), with the same coefficients on all 42 threads (K1, K3, and K4 post hoc). So
   one fugacity rule, the cusped threads themselves, cancels the divergence for every thread at once. This is
   Stanford and Yan's proposal, checked at tree level on the record's threads.
   - It is a proposal, not a theorem: off-shell topologies might cancel the divergence instead (their footnote 4).
   - Their one-loop form is not checked here.
3. **One universe per tower.** The finite part of each thread's slope count is 1 to 10⁻³ (K3a). Regularized, each
   tower of closed universes counts as one universe: the thread.
4. **The cusp's modular invariant at tree level.** The finite part of the log term carries log(√(Im τ)·|η(τ)|²) of
   each thread's cusp (K3c). That is the invariant Stanford and Yan find in the cusp's one-loop determinant.
5. **The renormalized ensemble is defined only up to adding a multiple of the cusped ensemble.**
   - In this scheme Z_ren is negative at s ≤ 2. Its sign is the scheme's, as Stanford and Yan's fugacity is negative.
   - The tick's class ±LR carries the largest single tower at every s read.
   - The Weeks manifold leads only at weak gravity, where e^{−s·0.9427} outgrows every multiple of e^{−s·2.03}.
     At s = 4 its term is still 13%.
6. **Weave or thread.** A weave result under the rule's three conditions: every thread of W122's rule and every slope
   to Q = 16 000; the sum over every closed universe they fill; and one counterterm rule for all threads at once. The
   towers' finite parts, K5, are thread results.

**Beside it, a READING: the c = 24 lead closed on W48** (relay §208; nothing new computed).
- The cusp's unit 1/Δ = η⁻²⁴ has weight −12: 24 chiral bosons with no zero modes. W48 counts it as three.
- Pure gravity at c = 24 sums every SL(2, ℤ) image of the vacuum q⁻¹. Regularized by Rademacher, that sum is J + 12

**Scope.** Tree level only. One loop and higher, off-shell topologies, manifolds with more than one cusp and the scale s

## W124.   traceless (TT) modes of the space.
- The least closed universe from the record's threads is the Weeks manifold, and the next is the Meyerhoff manifold, a
  filling of the tick itself (W122). The gravity line named their graviton spectrum and did not compute it.

- The rule (`W124_RULE.md`, bcc3686a3) was committed and pushed before the script. It disclosed the literature read
  for calibration (Cornish and Spergel; Inoue; Lin and Lipnowski) and the instrument checks.
- The script was reviewed (two fixes before its commit) and committed (8a2e3ed4b). It was run once, in 13 minutes. Its
  output (6e4ffb620) was committed unread, then read once.
- At the owner's request to verify, an independent adversarial review was run. A fresh agent was given the code and
  the rules, not the conclusions. Its findings are below with this seat's checks of them.

**The result (COMPUTED; G2 failed as worded; G5 held as worded, but its read-out was biased).**
- **G0.** The instrument checks:
  - O(3,1) defects are 10⁻¹⁴, and the vertex inequalities hold to 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ with the farthest vertex at r_out.
  - Lattice counts are within 0.7% of the volume law at ρ = 5, 6 and 7 on both manifolds.
  - The unfolding identity, checked directly: for the shortest geodesics, Σ|axis ∩ D| equals 2 × multiplicity ×
    length to 8 digits on both manifolds. On Weeks these are 0.5846, 0.7941 and 1.2899, each ×3.
  - 24.8 and 23.2 million elements were visited, and 124 352 and 119 851 axes kept.
- **G1.** For h = z^{a−2}(dx dy + dy dx), μ(a) = −a² + 2a + 2, and Ric₁ ∝ τ²T'' + 3τT' + a(2 − a)T, that is
  (μ − 2)T. With a = 1 + iν, μ = ν² + 3.
- **G2 FAILED** (part a).
  - (a) The constant mode at T = 0 gives 6.1335 (Weeks) and 6.1225 (Meyerhoff) against 6.1604. The deficits, 0.44%
    and 0.62%, exceed the tolerance of 0.1%.
  - (b) Weeks's scalar spectral function agrees with Cornish and Spergel's 74 eigenvalues, smoothed by the same window,
    to 0.045 on [0, 7].
  - (c) Meyerhoff's scalar count reaches 0.5 at 5.02.
- **G3.** Weeks has S₁ ≤ 0.021 on [0, 1], with its first coexact peak at t ≈ 3.14 (λ* ≈ 9.9, above Lin and
  Lipnowski's bound 8.9). Meyerhoff has S₁(0) = 1.369, against 1.38 for one eigenvalue at their λ₁* ≈ 0.33.
- **G4.** S₂ ≥ 0.0059 (Weeks) and ≥ 0.398 (Meyerhoff) on [0, 10].
- **G5, held as worded:** N₂ reaches 0.5 at 1.66, inside [1, 4]. The statistic is biased; see below.
- **G6.** N₂(8) is 19.18 against Weyl's 19.36 (Weeks), and 21.40 against 20.15 (Meyerhoff).
- **G7 (read-out).** Weeks has TT peaks at 2.65 (height 3.18) and 6.02 (6.58). Meyerhoff has a TT peak at 1.81
  (1.41), and S₂(0) = 0.398.

**What failed, and the checks after the read-out (post hoc, labelled).**
1. **G2(a)'s tolerance was wrong by design.**
   - The rule said that cutting at |u| ≤ R costs e⁻⁸. But the geodesic count grows like e^{2ℓ} and the weight falls
     like e^{−ℓ}. So the constant mode's geometric weight is a Gaussian in ℓ centred at 1/w² = 2.25 with spread 1.5,
     and the cut at 6 drops 0.038 (0.62%).
   - Re-enumerated, with cuts at 5.0, 5.5 and 6.0: the deficits are 0.191, 0.080 and 0.027 (Weeks) and 0.199, 0.093
     and 0.038 (Meyerhoff), against the main term's 0.206, 0.093 and 0.038. Cornish and Spergel's agreement tightens
     from 0.19 to 0.09 to 0.045 with the cut.

     The TT peaks stay at 2.64 to 2.65 and 1.80 to 1.81, and N₂ agrees to 10⁻³.
   - So the failure is the scalar constant mode's tail, not the calibration. The review found the same and checked it
     on its own reduced enumerations.
2. **G5's statistic was biased** (found by the review; checked by this seat).
   - The point where the smoothed count reaches 0.5 sits below the lowest eigenvalue: by 0.45 for a double one. The
     scalar side shows it, 4.80 against Cornish and Spergel's 5.18.
   - Positivity gives a bound instead. Since S₂(T) = Σ h_T(ν_k) with every term ≥ 0, a lowest eigenvalue ν₁ needs
     G(T − ν₁) + G(T + ν₁) ≤ S₂(T) + ε at every T.
   - Weeks: ν₁ ≥ 2.28 (ε = 0), 2.07 (ε = 0.01) and 1.97 (ε = 0.02). Meyerhoff: ν₁ ≥ 1.20, 1.19 and 1.18.
   - So 1.66 is not the lowest graviton, and the bound replaces it.
   - Meyerhoff's S₂(0) = 0.398 is what one mode at ν = 1.20 gives (0.396), a fit, not a proof.
3. **The review's other points, accepted.**
   - "No growing graviton" is a theorem (helicity ±2 has no complementary series), which G4 cannot test. It checks
     the normalization only.
   - The TT formula has no correction for any b₁, since the trivial character has only θ-modes 0 and ±1. The coexact
     factor 2 undoes Lin and Lipnowski's ½; the rule's "doubled to sum both helicities" misdescribes it.
   - The dedup key's rounding re-finds the identity six times at depth 2. It is filtered, and G0's duplicate check saw
     only kept elements.

**What it shows (READING; recorded, not banked, per the rule).**
1. **On the Milne cone over the Weeks manifold,** every graviton is τ⁻¹cos(ν_k log τ + φ), with discrete ν_k and no
   growing or zero mode.

   - About three modes cluster near ν ≈ 2.65, and the next weight is near 6.
2. **The tick's own closed universe, the Meyerhoff manifold, has a lower graviton:** ν₁ ≥ 1.18, with one mode near
   1.20 fitting the data.
3. **No G and no scale.** The frequencies are in curvature units.
4. **The instrument is calibrated by two outside sources:** Cornish and Spergel (scalars) and Lin and Lipnowski
   (coexact 1-forms, on both manifolds).

**Weave or thread.** Thread results, each one filled thread, chosen by W122's stated rule; the slope is a choice.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run). G2 failed as worded, on the constant mode's tail, which the rule's
tolerance did not allow for. G5's read-out was biased and is replaced by the positivity bound. Both were diagnosed
post hoc, the second by an independent review. The TT read-out is recorded, not banked. No data, so not a trial.
0 of 19.

## W123. The Higgs route to the cusp's unit (the owner's choice): a Higgs at weight 3/2 exists only with a unit at the weave's cusp; the least end data that make room for one is one unit on one eigenline, and the least pole is v₊'s, whose Higgs is ∂R; that end datum carries one chiral generation, not three (`the_higgs_route.py`; `W123_RULE.md`; post hoc `the_higgs_route_posthoc.py`)

  a Higgs would force the unit.

  generated by T, which keeps each of its eigenlines. This arc reads every per-line end datum in a box, for both hands.

- The rule (`W123_RULE.md`, bcc3686a3) was committed and pushed before the script.
- The script was reviewed against the rule (four fixes before its commit, among them the dual's lower bound and the
  "least pole" direction) and committed (8a2e3ed4b). It was run once, in 28 s. Its output (28a2c4bd3) was committed
  unread, then read once.

**The result (COMPUTED; five of seven cells as predicted; Y2 and Y6 failed as worded).**
- **Y0.** ρ = (e^{iπ/4}P, e^{iπ/4}L⁻¹) satisfies the braid relation with ρ(S)² = i. This seat's own exact series for R
  has line orders ⅛ on the ⅛ line, ⅜ on the ⅜ line and −⅛ on v₊ (the ⅞ line). It satisfies the weight −½ equations
  to 2.9 × 10⁻³¹.
- **Y1.** No unit, no Higgs: d(m) = 0 for all eight end data with every m_j ≤ 0.
- **Y2 FAILED as worded.** The counts gave d − h¹ = Σm in 55 of 64 end data for ρ and 54 of 64 for ρ̄_T.
  - Every failure has a double pole on some line, and a singular value between 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁰ and 10⁻⁹ that the run's

    3.4 × 10⁻¹⁶, and the kept ones at least 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁰. With the threshold in that gap (10⁻¹²) the law
    d − h¹ = Σm holds for every one. The cells Y1, Y3 and the uniform unit's count are unchanged.
- **Y3.** One unit on one line: d = 1 and h¹ = 0 for each of the three lines, with null values near 2 × 10⁻¹⁶.
- **Y4.** ∂R = q dR/dq + E₂R/24 has line orders ⅛, ⅜ and −⅛ and satisfies the weight-3/2 equations to 5.5 × 10⁻³¹.
  The section of the space for m = (0, 0, 1) has the same leading orders. With Y3, that space is ℂ·∂R.

  - For ρ̄_T at weight ½ (exponents ⅛, ⅝, ⅞), Y1 holds, each single-line unit gives d = 1 and h¹ = 0, with poles
    −⅞, −⅜ and −⅛, and the least is again on the ⅞ line.
  - Post hoc, the law holds for all 64.
- **Y7 (read-out).** Only the ⅛ line is a parity line; v₊ and the ⅜ line are combinations of e_j and e_k. The
  uniform unit gives d = 3 and h¹ = 0, B1700's three-dimensional space.

**What it shows (the rule's fixed meaning, with Y2's law as checked post hoc).**
1. **The Higgs, the unit and the chiral count are one datum.** A Higgs at weight 3/2 exists only with a unit at the
   cusp.
2. **The hierarchy's Higgs is the least Higgs.** The least end data that make room for a Higgs is one unit on one
   line. The least pole is v₊'s, and its Higgs is ∂R, the one with the hierarchy (B1700).
3. **That end datum carries one chiral generation, not three.** Its four-dimensional count is −χ = −1. Three needs
   Σm = 3, which a generation-blind source supplies (the uniform unit, W46's reading) and minimality does not.
4. **So route 1 does not force three.** Under GENESIS PF1 read on the index, or GENESIS PF2 read at the end, with least
   remainder, a forced Higgs forces one unit, on v₊, and one generation. That sharpens GENESIS FK10's question to

5. **A READING (by hand, from Y5 and Y7).** The least-pole line v₊ is not a parity line. So the least Higgs's end

    the three Higgs directions.

  carry GENESIS FK10 to GENESIS FK15. If the field's existence is forced and the unit is O(δ), the three follows. What
  remains open is what forces the field.

  - Every weight-3/2 form is c₀R + c₁∂R + c₂∂²R with cⱼ ∈ Δ⁻ᴺℂ[E₄, E₆], and d(m) is the kernel of an exact rational

  - At N = 3 and N = 4 it agrees with the threshold check in all 64 end data and differs from the run exactly where
    the run's threshold failed.
  - d(1,1,1) = 3 and d(2,2,2) = 6. The section for (0, 0, 1) equals ∂R exactly, compared to x⁶⁰.
  - ρ_R is W45's ρ_T: the intertwiner space is one-dimensional and invertible.

**Weave or thread.** WEAVE-type, as W45 and W46: the moves' joint representation, every per-line end datum in the box
at the weave's own cusp, and claims about the weave's surface.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; five of seven cells as predicted; Y2 and Y6 failed as worded on the
instrument's threshold, and the law they test holds post hoc). No data, so not a trial. 0 of 19.

## W120. From three dimensions to four (the owner's main task): the record's Λ = −1 is exactly the condition for every thread to be the space of a 4d vacuum universe, where gravitons propagate; read through the records' torus as a fibre, 4d gravity is a field on the τ-line, the moves force Im τ·|η|⁴, each pinched record is a cosmic string, and on a closed base the units come in twelves (`the_three_to_four.py`; `W120_RULE.md`; post hoc `the_three_to_four_posthoc.py`)

**Why.**
- **The owner's order** (2026-10-22): "GO FOR IT!", then "That's your main task now". The question: what carries the
  record's 3d gravity, which has no gravitons, to 4d gravity with propagating ones.
- **What the record had.** Every state is a 3d Einstein space with Λ = −1, family-wide (the fifth-force note, §3.2).
  A spin-2 field sits in E₆(−26), which no inner involution reaches (main's B1140, B1265). There is no G, no 4d Λ and
  no dynamics, since the framework has no dimensionful quantity, by theorem.
- **Why 3d gravity has no gravitons.** A graviton has d(d − 3)/2 polarizations: 0 at d = 3 and 2 at d = 4.

**The order.**
- The rule (`W120_RULE.md`, d86762158) was committed and pushed before the script. It disclosed one instrument check:
  b++LR gives 2.0298832128 and m004.
- The script (d88e9b321) was reviewed against the rule and run once. The output (45dea63a5) was committed unread,
  then read once.
- The post hoc check (13cf7a5c2, output bceb98b55) was written after the read, and is labelled.

**The result (COMPUTED; A1, A2 and B1 to B5 as predicted; A3 and A4 failed as worded on the instrument's notation).**
- **A1 (exact).** Over the curvature −1 metric g on the upper half-space, −dt² + a(t)²g has:
  - Ric = 0 for a = t;
  - Ric = 3g₄ for a = sinh t;
  - Ric = −3g₄ for a = sin t.
- **A2 (exact).** For g_κ = (dx² + dy² + dz²)/(1 + κr²/4)², which is Einstein with Ric = 2κg, the cone −dt² + t²g_κ
  is Ricci-flat iff κ = −1.
  - Every component is a multiple of κ + 1, for example R_xx = 32(κ + 1)/(κr² + 4)².
  - The cone is not flat at κ = 0, 1 or −2.
- **A3 (failed as worded).** b-+LR identifies as m001, a non-orientable manifold of volume 1.8319311884, not m003.
  - The rule read SnapPy's b-+w as the orientable bundle with monodromy −w. In SnapPy the first sign after b is
    orientability, and the second is the sign of the trace.
  - Post hoc: b++LR is m004, b+-LR is m003, and b-+LR and b--LR are both m001, non-orientable.
- **A4 (failed as worded, for the same reason).**
  - All 448 manifolds (224 words × 2) were geometric and agreed at high precision.
  - But the least volume, 1.8319311884, is the non-orientable b-+LR.
  - On the half the rule named correctly (b++w, orientable, positive trace), the least volume is +LR alone,
    2.0298832128, with +LLR and +LRR next at 2.6667.
- **A5 (read-out).** 154 distinct volumes; the largest is 9.6688. The two "signs" differ in volume, since one half was
  non-orientable.
- **Post hoc (labelled): the orientable census.** The bundles b++w and b+-w were taken over the same 224 words: 448
  manifolds, all geometric and checked.
  - The least volume, 2.029883212819307, is attained exactly at ±LR (m004 and m003).
  - Next come ±LLR and ±LRR at 2.666744783 (a gap of 0.637), then ±L³R and ±LR³ at 2.989, ±L⁴R at 3.177 and ±L⁵R at
    3.297.
  - The two trace signs agree in volume for every word.
  - So A4's intended claim holds post hoc.
- **B1 (exact).** The Euclidean metric e^φ|dz|² + (1/Im τ)|dx + τ dy|² is Ricci-flat for τ = z and for τ = z², with
  e^φ = Im τ·|e^{az}|². Both controls fail, as predicted: e^φ = (Im τ)², and the non-holomorphic τ = u + i(1 + v²).
- **B2.** Im τ·|η|⁴ changes under L and R by at most 3.9 × 10⁻⁴⁰ at 40 digits.
  - The controls Im τ alone and |η|⁴ alone change by 0.83 and 4.89.
  - Among (Im τ)^p|η|^{2q}, only (p, q) = (1, 2), (2, 4) and (3, 6) are invariant.
- **B3.** At a pinch (τ = log z/2πi) the exponent of |z| in |η|⁴ is 0.16670 at 10⁻⁴, 0.1666666683 at 10⁻⁸, and 1/6 to
  sixteen digits beyond. Gauss–Bonnet, at a deficit of 2π/12 per unit, gives 24 units for a sphere and 12 for a flat
  cylindrical end.
- **B4 (exact).** The map χ to ℤ/12 is a homomorphism on 200 random pairs.
  - χ(R) = 1, χ(L) = 11, χ(S) = 9, χ(−I) = 6 and χ(LR) = 0.
  - Every sampled conjugate of R has χ = 1.
  - (RL⁻¹)³ = −I and (RL⁻¹)⁶ = I.
- **B5.** 12 units for the rational elliptic surface and 24 for K3. The least positive count is 12.

**What it shows (a READING, given the stated hypotheses).**
1. **The cone: the thread as space.**
   - The record's normalization, Λ = −1 in three dimensions, is exactly the condition for each thread to be the space
     of an exact 4d vacuum universe: the flat Milne cone −dt² + t²g, an open Friedmann vacuum.
   - Over the same g, the scale factors sinh t and sin t give de Sitter and anti-de Sitter in their open slicings.
   - No choice and no free number enter besides the scale t, and gravitons with two polarizations propagate there.
     G is not supplied.
2. **The tick is least.** Among every thread's universe to length 10, the tick's ±LR has the least volume, uniquely
   (orientable, both trace signs; post hoc).
   - For closed spatial sections the volume is the 4d vacuum flow's energy at its attractor (Fischer and Moncrief;
     Andersson and Moncrief). So the tick's universe would be the ground state among threads.
   - The threads are cusped, outside those theorems' scope, so this part is a scope-limited READING.
   - With main's B1629, the tick is least both as a geodesic and as a universe.
3. **The fibre: 4d gravity on the τ-line.**
   - In the torus-fibred sector, 4d vacuum gravity is a field τ on the record's τ-line. In Lorentzian signature (the
     Gowdy class) its waves are the gravitational waves.
   - Invariance under the moves forces the base factor Im τ·|η|⁴.
4. **The pinched record is a cosmic string, and the units come in twelves.**
   - Where the records' torus pinches, the solution has a string of deficit 2π/12.
   - On a closed base, compactness forces such points. The moves' abelianization ℤ/12 makes their signed count a
     multiple of 12: 12 on the rational elliptic surface, 24 on K3.
   - The regular metric uses Δ/q, Δ times a simple pole at the cusp, which reads as W47's unit inside a 4d metric. So
     4d gravity, read through the fibre, supplies GENESIS FK10's units as physical sources, in twelves.
   - An observation: the tick LR is one twist of each hand (χ(R) = 1, χ(L) = −1), so it is neutral in ℤ/12.
5. **What it does not do.**
   - It chooses no carrier. Whether the records' torus is space or a fibre is GENESIS FK11's dictionary.
   - It gives no G, and no 4d Λ beyond the three maximally symmetric cases.
   - It computes no graviton spectrum.
   - It does not compute whether the twelve units give a chiral three. That is the triplet's index on the rational
     elliptic surface or K3, named here as W121.

**Weave or thread.**
- A1 and A2 are family-wide.
- A4 and its post hoc are a census of thread results, labelled so. Their one claim about all threads at once is which
  thread has the least volume.
- Part B is WEAVE-type: its quantities are defined by the moves' joint action on the shared fibre.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; seven cells as predicted; A3 and A4 failed as worded on the instrument's
notation, traced post hoc and labelled; A4's intended claim holds post hoc). No data, so not a trial. 0 of 19.

## W119. Beyond tree level (the third of the owner's three arcs): no Kähler metric moves θ̄'s structural zero, and running between the forced scale and M_Z moves the forced coefficients by a factor 0.55 to 1.13, too little to reach the down quarks' or the leptons' window (`the_beyond_tree_level.py`; `W119_RULE.md`)

**Why.** After W118, by the owner's order: the third arc, one step beyond the holomorphic tree level.
- W113 left θ̄ ∈ {0, π} at every τ by structure, in one forced assignment. W118 left exact rational double ratios
  m₁m₃/m₂² near ω, two of them in the up quarks' window and none in the down quarks' or the leptons'.
- **The question.** Do the corrections beyond tree level change either result?
  - **Part K, the Kähler correction.** The matter fields' metrics, which the holomorphic couplings do not fix.
    Canonical normalization replaces Y by K_L^{−1/2} Y K_R^{−1/2}, which multiplies det Y by a positive real number.
    So arg det(Y_u Y_d) is unchanged by every Hermitian positive metric. This was derived by hand in the rule and
    checked here.
  - **Part L, the loops.** The one-loop running of the double ratio between the scale where the forced structure
    holds, Λ, and M_Z. DR(M_Z) = F · DR(Λ), with F = exp(−∫ c(y) dt / 16π²) driven by the third generation's
    Yukawas, in the SM and the MSSM.
- **Cited, not redone:** the one-loop potential for τ (W59), and main's B1686 (nothing computed holds τ).

**The order.**
- The rule (`W119_RULE.md`) was committed and pushed first (403bf62b7), with relay §185.
- The script was committed before its one run (7144030fe), and its output before it was read (1423a23a5).

**Disclosed.**
- W113, W114, W118, W59 and main's B1686 were seen before the rule. The β functions were recalled, not re-derived.
  The rough size of the running was estimated by hand before the rule (F of order e^{±0.5}).
- While the script was written, its code paths were run in scratch only on random matrices and on a toy equation,
  dy/dt = y³, whose blow-up time is exact.
- **What the dev test changed, before the run.** On random hierarchical matrices, float64 rounding alone moved
  arg det by up to 8 × 10⁻³, against 5 × 10⁻³⁸ at 50 digits. So B1 is decided at 50 digits, with each K^{−1/2} made
  exactly Hermitian in float64, and the float64 change is reported beside it. A non-Hermitian control, which must move
  the phase by 0.6, is reported too. The script's docstring states this.

**The result (COMPUTED; one run; every cell as predicted).**

| cell | prediction | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B0 | the control: the MSSM's gauge couplings meet within 2% at 2 × 10¹⁶ GeV; the SM's spread is above 5% | 90% | **held** — MSSM 0.17% (g ≈ 0.719); SM 10.6% |
| B1 | the Kähler theorem: arg det(Y_u Y_d) changes by less than 10⁻¹² under every sampled metric, at three τ | 99% | **held** — worst 7.3 × 10⁻⁴⁸ at 50 digits over 300 metrics; the control moves it by 0.6 at every τ |
| B2 | the band: F in [0.4, 2.5] for each sector at every kept point | 85% | **held** — all 24 points kept; up 0.545 to 0.903, down 0.702 to 1.130, leptons 0.843 to 1.000 |
| B3 | **no coherent point;** no forced coefficient reaches the leptons' window at any point | 95% | **held** — none coherent; nothing reaches the leptons' window or the down quarks' |
| B4 | read-out: each sector's range of F, and which coefficient reaches which window where | — | up: 385/529 at all 24 points, 3/5 at 23, W68's 1 at the 21 MSSM points, 5/4 at 5; down and leptons: none |

- **The float64 read-out** of B1 is up to 1.3 × 10⁻¹² (at τ = 0.05 + 1.6i). That is above the cell's 10⁻¹² from
  rounding alone; the 50-digit decision, fixed before the run, is what B1 reads.
- **No Yukawa approaches √(4π).** The largest at any Λ is y_t ≈ 1.03 (the MSSM at tan β = 2 and 10¹⁶ GeV).

**The margins (arithmetic on the read-outs, after the run; not a cell).**
- **The down quarks.** The forced coefficients nearest the window (1.81 to 3.97) are 5/4 and 735/121 ≈ 6.07.
  - 5/4 rises at most to 1.41, at F = 1.13.
  - 735/121 falls at least to 4.27, at F = 0.702. It would need F ≤ 0.654, which no scan point gives.
- **The leptons.** The smallest forced coefficient, 3/5, falls at least to 0.51 (window 0.061 to 0.107). It would
  need F ≤ 0.18.
- **The up quarks.** Every scan point brings two to four coefficients into the window. Its width (a factor 2.4) and
  the band of F make that uninformative, as in W118.

**What it shows.**
- **θ̄'s structural zero is safe beyond tree level.** No Kähler metric, minimal or not, τ-dependent or not, moves
  arg det(Y_u Y_d); B1 checks the theorem at three τ. With the literature cited in the rule (θ̄'s running is of high
  loop order and negligible), W113's structural θ̄ stays structural. The assignment that has it still does not fit
  the quarks (W113, W114).
- **W118's negative stands beyond tree level.** One-loop running moves the forced double ratios by a factor 0.55 to
  1.13 across the SM and the MSSM (tan β 2 to 50, Λ 10¹² to 10¹⁶ GeV). The gap between the forced values 5/4 and
  735/121 still covers the down quarks' window. The leptons' 0.081 lies more than a factor of six below every forced
  value after running.
- **What would change it lies outside the frame.** Non-minimal Kähler terms carry their own free coefficients (Chen,
  Ramos-Sánchez and Ratz, arXiv:1909.06910). They can move masses and mixings, but they add free numbers and cannot
  lower the count. Read with W118, the forced rationals are predictions only if the Kähler metric is minimal.
- The departure from the symmetric points stays unexplained at one loop (W59, B1686).

**Post hoc, after main's B1693 opened (S162; arithmetic on two committed outputs; not a cell).**
- B1693 compared B1692's bound (one Higgs splits the sectors' m₂/m₃ by at most four) with the data at M_Z: T1 is
  excluded (the leptons over the up quarks, 15.98) and T2 is allowed (the down-lepton pair, 3.14).
- Carried to the frame's scale with W119's factors (`the_b1693_at_the_frame_scale.py`), over the 24 scan points:
  - T1 becomes 17.7 to 29.3, so the running strengthens the exclusion;
  - T2 becomes 2.78 to 3.84, still within the bound.
- So B1693's verdict does not depend on the scale at which it is read, in either cell.
- *Scope, added later the same day (main's S167):* B1692's bound and B1693's exclusion hold for B1653's point
  coupling, the large-L limit. At the canonical end one Higgs is not excluded. This check is arithmetic on the
  large-L values and says nothing about the canonical end (relay §193).

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; every cell as predicted). A WEAVE-type result given the frames: Part K
is about every Kähler metric on the weave's matter, and Part L takes every forced coefficient on record at every scan
point. 0 of 19.

## W118. The first generation (the second of the owner's three arcs): the composite field, the fermions' own bilinear, lifts the first generation's zero with a forced power and an exact rational coefficient; two coefficients fall in the up quarks' window, but none in the down quarks' or the leptons', so no coherent assignment exists (`the_first_generation.py`; `W118_RULE.md`)

  (c), end data at the puncture, needs P-108's parent map. (e), the exponential sector, was never built. Both stay

  P₁ = S₂ × S₃, P₂ = S₃ × S₁ and P₃ = S₁ × S₂. They are paired by B1644's form with W68's seven sections and with

  | --- | --- | --- |

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; H0–H2 as predicted; H4 failed, closed by arithmetic after the run). A
WEAVE-type result, given Λ (GENESIS FK11) and the stated hypotheses (B1644's form, H-sec, H-pair′, H-comp). 0 of 19.

## W117. A point on the line (the first of the owner's three arcs): the weave's canonical functionals, extremized along each thread's closed geodesic, mark the tick's line only at i, where the masses are degenerate; a quarter of the other lines carry a mark that holds the quarks with two degrees of freedom, which no rule selects (`the_points_on_the_line.py`; `W117_RULE.md`)

first.
- W116 found that a line is too weak a mark at the data's precision, so the seed would have to mark a point.
- **The mechanism,** fixed in the rule before any comparison: τ is held on a thread's closed geodesic (W116) and
  settles where a canonical weave functional (W51) is extremal along it. That means the local minima of e₁, e₂, N_T
  and P_T, and the local maxima of D = y|η|⁴.
- At a mark τ is fixed, so W114's zero-dof assignments 11, 13 and 14 keep two degrees of freedom (pass mark 5.99).

**The order.**
- The rule (`W117_RULE.md`) was committed and pushed first (19a6e1994), with relay §180.
- The script was committed before its one run (67d6503c5), and its output before it was read (2b84d4e88).

**Disclosed.**
- W116's whole record was seen before the rule, and so were W51's table and main's B1636.
- While the script was written, its code paths were run in scratch only on three lines of length 9, outside the
  census, against synthetic targets.
- The script places a CP-fixed mark exactly on its reflection line, where symmetry puts it. The refinement had found
  it within about 10⁻⁸; its docstring states this.

**The result (COMPUTED; one run; every cell as predicted).**

| cell | prediction | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R0 | the structure: the census as in W116; W51's closed forms at i and ω; e₃ = 4 at every mark; F = 8 on the tick's line; every mark critical | 95% | **held** — the closed forms to 3 × 10⁻¹⁵, e₃ and F to 10⁻¹⁴, every mark critical to 7 × 10⁻⁸; 205 marks on the 34 classes |
| R1 | the controls: W115's solutions reproduced; synthetic data fitted back at a mark | 80% | **held** — every solution reproduced; the control at a mark of LLRLLRLR's line to χ² 10⁻²⁶ |
| R2 | J = 0 at every CP-fixed mark | 97% | **held** — \|J\| ≤ 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁵ over 1140 couplings |
| R3 | the tick's marks are only its CP-fixed points | 70% | **held** — one mark, i, where all five functionals are extremal |
| R4 | **the tick fails** at its marks | 90% | **held** — χ² 1310 to 1378 at i for 11, 13 and 14, at both budgets |
| R5 | at least one line passes | 40% | **held** — 10 of the 40 lines, best χ²_line 1.07 |
| R6 | **the null:** p ≥ 0.05 | 90% | **held** — p = 0.90 |
| R7 | read-out: assignment 16 at the tick's mark | — | χ² 1244 at i, with 0 dof |

- **The tick's line is marked only at i.** Every functional is extremal along it there, and there only. At the
  elliptic point the couplings give degenerate pairs (W50), so no assignment comes near the data.
- **Eleven lines are marked only at a CP-fixed point:** LR, LLR, LLLR, LLRR, L⁴R, L⁵R, L³R³, L⁶R, L⁴RLR, L⁷R and
  L⁴R⁴. Their marks fail.
- **The other 23 classes carry generic marks:** 117 were fitted, after the CP-mirror copies. All 136 fitted marks
  sit low in F, at Im τ from 0.866 to 1.08, between i and ω, where W51's functionals pull.
- **Ten lines pass** (25%), at 39 passing marks, counting the CP-mirror marks on each line. 32 of those are
  assignment 11's, 4 are 14's and 3 are 13's.
  - Most sit just off i, at Im τ ≈ 1.00 to 1.02 and |Re τ| ≈ 0.07 to 0.22, with J between 0.8 and 3.1 × 10⁻⁵. A
    few sit near ω.
  - The best is LLLRLLRR's local minimum of N_T at −0.211 + 1.016i (assignment 14, χ² 1.07).
  - **LLLRR's line, a read-out:** the global marks of e₁, N_T and D on this length-5 line all pass, at ±0.20 + 1.02i
    (χ² 1.09 to 1.35). It is noted, not claimed: choosing it would be a hand-pick unless the principle names
    LLLRR.
- **One passing mark is CP-fixed: J = 0 there.** It is LLRLLRR's at −½ + 0.913i (assignment 13, χ² 4.24). The
  record's quark χ² (W66's eight observables) contains no CP phase. Its moduli at a = 0.10 allow J from zero to about
  the measured value, so a CP-conserving point can pass. The measured J (about 3 × 10⁻⁵) excludes this mark, but the
  fit does not see it.

**What it shows.**
- **The seed's own line, settled by the weave's functionals, lands on the weave's symmetric point i,** where the
  masses are degenerate. By the rule fixed in advance, R4 and R3 hold: a clean negative for the tick, and the reason
  is structural.
- **The functionals do mark points off the symmetric ones on most other lines,** and a quarter of the lines carry a
  mark that holds the quarks with two degrees of freedom. Each of those is one thread's mark, and nothing on record
  names the thread. So choosing one would be a hand-pick, and nothing is claimed. The count does not move. 0 of 19.
- **A lesson for the frame (a READING).** The record's fits use eight moduli and never the CP phase, so a fit cannot
  tell CP violation from its absence at this allowance. Every later fit should add J (or the angle β) to the
  observables. That also bears on W114 and W116, whose fits never tested J. Their passing points had J ≈ 2 to
  3 × 10⁻⁵, near the measured value, but as a consequence of the moduli, not as a test.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; every cell as predicted). A census of thread results with weave
functionals, labelled so. A clean negative for the tick, and no evidence from the other lines. 0 of 19.

## W116. The seed's marks (the owner's choice after W115): on every thread's closed geodesic up to length 8, W114's zero-dof quark assignments keep a fit with a degree of freedom to spare, the tick's line among them, so the seed's line costs nothing and selects nothing (`the_seed_geodesics.py`; `W116_RULE.md`)

**Why.** After W115 the owner chose the seed as the source of the departure (main's P-224 and P-225).
- **The mechanism,** fixed in the rule before any comparison: τ lies on a thread's closed geodesic, the one line its
  word's matrix leaves invariant. The seed fixes the line, and the point along it is one fitted number.
- **On a line,** W114's zero-dof assignments 11, 13 and 14 keep one degree of freedom, so a fit there is a test.
- **The census:** every thread up to length 8, which is 69 words tracing 40 lines (34 up to the CP mirror). The
  tick's line (LR) is one row, and the others are its null.

**The order.**
- The rule (`W116_RULE.md`) was committed and pushed first (e34f9f9d1), with relay §178.
- The script was committed before its one run (57491e223), and its output before it was read (61efe388b).

**Disclosed.**
- W115's whole record was seen before the rule, including every quark solution's τ. The rule disclosed a hand check:
  the tick's line misses every W115 solution, the nearest by 0.044 in Im τ. That check proved a poor guide (below).
- While the script was written, its code paths were run in scratch only on a line outside the census (LLRLRRLRR,
  length 9), against synthetic targets.
- The script closes the warm starts under the CP mirror (−τ̄ with the same coefficients, which maps a solution to a
  solution), so that mirror lines get the same starts. Its docstring states this.

**The result (COMPUTED; one run; S4 failed; the other cells as predicted).**

| cell | prediction | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S0 | the structure: 69 words, 40 lines, 34 classes; every axis invariant; M(w)ᵀ the reversed mirror's matrix; B1636's golden spectrum on the tick's line; one mirror pair's observables equal | 95% | **held** — the invariance to 5 × 10⁻¹⁴, the golden spectrum to 6 × 10⁻¹⁶, the mirror pair to 10⁻¹³ |
| S1 | the controls: W115's solutions and W114's point for 16 reproduced; synthetic data fitted back on a line | 80% | **held** — every solution to 10⁻⁶; the control on LLLLLRR's line to χ² 1.3 × 10⁻⁵ |
| S2 | J = 0 at the tick's two CP-fixed points, i and ½ + i√5/2 | 97% | **held** — \|J\| ≤ 5 × 10⁻¹⁶ there, against 0.002 to 0.04 at a generic point of the line |
| S3 | every assignment not fitted stays above its pass mark on a line | 99% | **held** — the closest is W114's 15 (8.18 against 3.84) |
| S4 | **the tick:** no assignment passes on the tick's line | 85% | **failed** — 11 passes at χ² 0.33 and 13 at 1.09; 14 does not (5.55) |
| S5 | at least one line passes for the family | 70% | **held** — all 40 lines pass, with χ²_fam from 0.0013 to 2.96 |
| S6 | **the null:** p ≥ 0.05 | 85% | **held** — p = 0.60: 24 of the 40 lines do as well as the tick or better |
| S7 | read-out: assignment 16 on every line | — | exact (χ² ≤ 10⁻⁶) on 17 lines at the census budget, and on the tick's at the larger one |

- **Per assignment** (census budget): 11 passes on 30 lines, 13 on 28 and 14 on 38; 16 is compatible on 36.
- **The tick's best points sit next to i,** the elliptic point its line passes through:
  - 11 at 0.072 + 1.033i;
  - 13 at ±0.0097 + 1.0048i (a CP-mirror pair, one from each budget);
  - an exact fit of 16 at 0.0015 + 1.0007i.
- **The census budget is an upper bound.** On the tick the larger budget lowered 14 from 8.32 to 5.55, and 16 from
  3.79 to an exact fit. Every line had already passed, so S5 and S6 do not depend on it.
- **Why the hand check misled.** Missing W115's exact solutions does not mean failing.
  - With one degree of freedom left, a fit tolerates a distance of about 0.04 or more to the nearest solution: the
    tick's line passes at 0.038.
  - Every line of the census comes within 0.062 of a solution (median 0.007), in hyperbolic distance on the modular
    surface.
  - Across the lines, log χ²_fam and that distance correlate (r = 0.57).

**What it shows.**
- **The seed's line costs nothing and selects nothing.** In this frame the quark data, at W66's allowance, hold τ
  only to a region about 0.05 across around each zero-dof solution. Every thread's line up to length 8 crosses such a
  region, so the degree of freedom a line buys tests nothing.
- **By the rule fixed in advance:** S4 failed and S6 held. "The tick's line holds the quarks, but so do enough other
  lines. That is no evidence, as in W112." The count does not move. 0 of 19.
- **A line is too weak a mark at this precision; the seed would have to mark the point.** The only points the line
  marks itself are its CP-fixed ones, where J = 0 (S2). So the departure along the line stays a fitted number. On the
  tick's line it is small (the fits sit 0.002 to 0.08 from i), as the goal page's reading has it, and its size is
  fitted.
- **Two corrections of scope.**
  - W115 is unaffected: its joint fit let τ move freely.
  - Relay §177 noted that every rigid fit misses with m_s/m_b too large and |V_cb| too small. W116's one-dof fits
    reach both (pulls 0.06 and 0.32 on the tick), so that miss belongs to the rigid assignments, not to the frame.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; S4 failed, the other cells as predicted). A census of thread results,
labelled so. Every thread's line up to length 8 is taken, and the claims are about all of them. But each fit is one
thread's, so THE WEAVE's condition 2 fails; the rule says why no weave version exists. No evidence. 0 of 19.

## W115. The leptons at the shared τ (the owner's choice after W114): at every τ the quark fits pin, no lepton coupling with one free number reaches the charged leptons; m_μ/m_τ stays above 0.21, and random targets fare as well (`the_shared_tau.py`; `W115_RULE.md`)

**Why.** After W114 the owner chose the leptons at the shared τ.
- A zero-dof quark fit pins τ, and τ is one modulus for every sector.
- The charged leptons, coupled at that τ with one free number for two ratios, then make one prediction that the
  quarks cannot make.

**The order.**
- The rule (`W115_RULE.md`) was committed and pushed first (5a9914425), with relay §176.
- The script was committed before its one run (79d7ad5eb), and its output before it was read (6d5e09598).

**Disclosed.**
- W114's whole record was seen before the rule, and so was the lepton data, to write the ratios into it.
- While the script was written, its code paths were run in scratch only where they touch no cell. That included once
  at τ = 0.21 + 1.17i, which is not a quark solution. That run printed that no angle of T⊗T at weight 3 fits m_μ/m_τ
  exactly there, and printed no χ².

**The result (COMPUTED; one run; every cell as predicted).**

| cell | prediction | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V0 | the control is recovered by T1 to 10⁻⁶ and by T2 to 0.01 | 85% | **held** — 5 × 10⁻¹⁶ and 6 × 10⁻²¹ |
| V1 | the census: only T⊗T at 1 and 3, T̄⊗T̄ at 1, mixed at 0 and 2 have d ≤ 2; the d = 1 ones fail as stated | 95% | **held** — at every solution, T⊗T at 1 has m₂/m₁ ≈ 0.6, T̄⊗T̄ at 1 has m_e = 0, and mixed at 0 is degenerate; the two mixed orders agree to 6 × 10⁻¹⁶ |
| V2 | W114's best point is recovered as a solution for 11 and 13 | 95% | **held** — and for 14, W114's point (χ² 2.55) is reproduced but is not a solution, because exact ones exist (below) |
| V3 | no combination passes the pinned fit | 80% | **held** — the best χ²_ℓ,min is 163 |
| V4 | no combination passes the joint fit | 75% | **held** — the best is 109 |
| V5 | the null: p ≥ 0.05 | 85% | **held** — p = 0.507 |

- **The quark solutions** (χ²_q ≤ 10⁻⁶ for 11 and 13; ≤ 3.84 for 14):
  - **11:** three, at τ = 0.0513 + 1.0679i, 0.0159 + 1.1467i and −0.0529 + 1.0866i.
  - **13:** one pair, at τ = ±0.0687 + 1.5341i. The two are CP mirrors (τ ↔ −τ̄) with identical results.
  - **14:** an exact mirror pair, at τ = ±0.0856 + 1.1993i (χ²_q ≈ 10⁻¹⁹ and 10⁻¹⁶), and two compatible local minima,
    at −0.424 + 1.583i (2.55, W114's) and 0.5 + 1.685i (3.3).
- **Pinned** (18 combinations).
  - At every solution's best angle, m_e/m_μ lands on the data (0.0048), but m_μ/m_τ stays between 0.21 and 0.81,
    against 0.059.
  - Neither coupling reaches m_μ/m_τ = 0.059 at any angle, at any of the solutions.
  - T⊗T at 3 comes closest (χ² 163 to 547), and mixed at 2 is far (564 to 687).
- **Joint.** With τ free, the fit can only lower m_μ/m_τ to 0.137 (T⊗T at 3, assignment 14). It does so by moving τ
  up to 1.94i, which costs the quarks χ²_q = 38. The best total is 109.
- **The null.** Over 4000 random lepton targets within a decade of the data, the median family-best χ² is 154. The
  data's is 163 (p = 0.507), so the data sits at the median of chance.

**What it shows.**
- **The shared modulus predicts nothing for the leptons in this frame.** At every τ the zero-dof quark fits pin, no
  lepton coupling with a free number to spare reaches the charged leptons.
  - The miss is the heavy pair: m_μ/m_τ stays above 0.21.
  - These τ lie at Im τ ≈ 1.1–1.7, where the lepton couplings' second hierarchy has not yet opened.
- **By the rule fixed in advance:** V3 and V4 hold, a clean negative. The count does not move. 0 of 19.
- **A correction to W114, from W115's broader search.** Assignment 14 also fits the quarks exactly, at
  τ = ±0.0856 + 1.199i. W114's χ²_min of 2.55 was a local minimum. W114's verdict stands (14 was compatible
  either way), and its section carries a dated note.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; every cell as predicted). A WEAVE-type result, given the frame: every
compatible zero-dof quark assignment, every solution the stated search found, and every lepton coupling with a
prediction. A clean negative. 0 of 19.

## W114. The tuned layer's fit (the owner's choice after W113): with θ̄ = 0 at every τ, no assignment with a degree of freedom fits the quarks, and four with none are compatible; θ̄ = 0 and the quark data coexist in the frame only where the fit predicts nothing (`the_tuned_fit.py`; `W114_RULE.md`)

The question: can the frame hold the observed quarks with θ̄ = 0 at every τ at all?

  compatible assignment carries the Standard Model's ten quark numbers, and θ̄ = 0 is bought by the tunings. That is
  the Standard Model's own count with θ̄ tuned to zero.
- **By the rule fixed in advance:** U3 holds and U4 fails. Only assignments with as many parameters as observables
  reach the data. θ̄ = 0 is then compatible with the quarks in the frame, but the fit predicts nothing. The count does

- **What it leaves (a READING).** A zero-dof fit fixes τ, and τ is one modulus for every sector. So the lepton sector,
  coupled at the same τ, could make a prediction that the quark sector cannot. That would be a new arc with its own
  look-elsewhere count, and it is offered to the owner, not started.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; U4 failed, the rest held). A WEAVE-type result, given the frame: all
sixteen tuned assignments up to weight 7, none hand-picked. 0 of 19.

**Corrected 2026-10-21 (W115's broader search, labelled).** Assignment 14 also fits the quarks exactly, at
τ = ±0.0856 + 1.199i (χ²_q ≈ 10⁻¹⁹). The χ²_min of 2.55 above was a local minimum of this search. The verdict
stands: 14 was compatible either way, and U4 failed either way.

| T1 | every real root on each tuned variety pure and non-degenerate | 90% | **failed as worded** — 140 of 142, 87 of 88, 138 of 143, 135 of 139; post hoc, every exception is a rank-two member (m_min/m_max ≈ 10⁻³¹ at all three τ), and every non-degenerate root is pure (spread ≤ 1.4 × 10⁻²⁶) |
| T2 | J ≠ 0 in each of the 16 viable tuned assignments | 85% | **held** — 16 of 16, with \|J\| > 10⁻⁸ for 18 to 20 of 20 pairs |
| T3 | read-out: the smallest hierarchy measure | — | from 6.6 × 10⁻⁴ (T⊗T at 5 in both sectors) to 0.64 (with T⊗T at 1, B1636's sum rule) |

- **The census in one line.** With the counterterm and CP in the law, θ̄ is constant for every coupling only at one
  weight per type: k = 1 for T⊗T, k = 3 for T̄⊗T̄ and k = 0 for mixed. Among all weights, these are the only ones.
- **The one forced assignment.** Every quark field in T̄, at coupling weight 3 in both sectors. It is the hand
  opposite to the record's (B1640). Its anomaly is cancellable (W101 A2, with K = 6).
  - Its space is three-dimensional, and the up and down sectors draw on it with their own real coefficients.
  - Every member has det Y = 4096κ(c)·η¹⁸, with κ = −c₁³ + 3c₁c₂² + 3c₁c₃² − 3c₁c₂c₃ + 2c₂³ − 3c₂²c₃ − 3c₂c₃² + 2c₃³
    in the script's rational real basis.
  - **The cusp exponents** of the mass ratios for generic members are ¾ and 0: τ suppresses one mass by q^¾, and the
    other two are comparable. A second hierarchy needs a tuned coefficient in each sector.
- **The best fit** (C6), at τ = −3 × 10⁻⁷ + 1.854i, on the imaginary axis:

| observable | fit | data | pull |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| m_u/m_c | 0.00235 | 0.00198 | 0.85 |
| m_c/m_t | 0.00374 | 0.00368 | 0.14 |
| m_d/m_s | 0.075 | 0.050 | 2.68 |
| m_s/m_b | 0.056 | 0.0187 | 8.21 |
| \|V_us\| | 0.248 | 0.225 | 0.97 |
| \|V_cb\| | 0.028 | 0.042 | −3.89 |
| \|V_ub\| | 0.0026 | 0.0037 | −3.34 |
| \|V_td\| | 0.0095 | 0.0086 | 1.04 |

  - J there is 9 × 10⁻¹³, against the measured 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ (B1673). θ̄ there is π, a bit any one sector's sign flips.
  - The next stage-2 minima are 104.1, 104.5 and 108.5.

**What it shows.**
- **θ̄ = 0 and CP violation can coexist without tuning in the record's frame.** In exactly one assignment, θ̄ ∈ {0, π}
  at every τ while J ≠ 0 at every generic τ. N10's exclusivity, exact at weights 2 and 3 with the quarks in T (W101),
  is not a theorem of the frame: the opposite hand breaks it.
- **But that assignment does not fit the quarks.** χ²_min is 104 with two degrees of freedom, and 34 even at a 20%
  allowance. The worst miss is m_s/m_b, too large by a factor 3. The cusp exponents say why: one light mass per
  sector comes from τ, and the second hierarchy has to come from coefficients both sectors draw from one small space.
- **And its best point is CP-conserving.** The fit settles on the imaginary axis, where J vanishes. So at the data's
  best point, θ̄ = 0 and CP violation exclude each other again. This is a read-out, not a cell.
- **The tuned layer** keeps J ≠ 0 in all 16 tuned assignments, but each pays one tuned coefficient per tuned sector. It
  trades one real number for another and cannot lower the count.
- **By the rule fixed in advance:** F4, C2 and C3 hold, but C6 fails. θ̄ = 0 and the CKM phase are compatible without
  tuning in exactly one assignment, but that assignment does not fit the data. N10's exclusivity is broken
  structurally, not physically. The count does not move. 0 of 19.

**Status.** COMPUTED (the rule first; one run; C6 failed as predicted; T1 failed as worded, its exceptions classified
post hoc as rank-two members; the rest held). A WEAVE-type result, given the frame (W101's hypotheses and CP in the
law): every quark hand, every coupling weight, every coupling. 0 of 19.

## W111. The surface route (P-211), by hand: at genus g ≥ 2 the mapping classes fix no non-trivial SL(2, ℂ) character; the odd-p Heisenberg character is fixed at every genus; the 2-group one only at g = 1, as Q₈ (`W111_PROOF.md`; checks `the_surface_route.py`)

**Why.** Main's relay of 2026-10-21 (two records characterised, and the surface route, §4) asks this seat for a proof
of P-211, with checks committed before their run. The question is the other natural extension of the moves beyond
two records: a surface's own mapping classes, in place of every transvection (relay §168).

**The order.**
- The proof (`W111_PROOF.md`) was worked by hand and committed first (bfd9ffadc), with six checks, their expected
  outcomes and priors.
- The checks script was committed before its run (663a7904a), and its output before it was read (fdbec8e8e).

**Disclosed.**
- **An exploratory search came first.** It was run before the proof, to find an explicit move that mixes two handles.
  It found μ: a₁ ↦ γa₁, b₂ ↦ γb₂, with γ = b₁⁻¹a₂. Its script and output (`the_surface_route_exploration.py`) were
  committed with the proof.
- **Two launches wrote nothing.**
  - The first was killed by a container restart.
  - The second crashed in C5: the word helper began from a 2 × 2 identity, so the larger matrices of C5 and C6
    could not multiply.
  - Only the traceback was read; C1–C4's values went unread. A one-line fix was committed (4278ac3b1), and the third
    launch is the one run recorded.

**The theorem (PROVED).** F_{2g} is free on a₁, b₁, …, a_g, b_g, with boundary word ∂ = ∏[a_k, b_k]. The moves of
the surface route are the automorphisms keeping ∂'s class: the mapping classes (Zieschang).
- **(a)** For g ≥ 2, an SL(2, ℂ) character fixed by the handle twists and the adjacent handle swaps is trivial.
  - Each handle is trivial or quaternion (W109 (ii)).
  - A quaternion handle forces every other generator to ±I, through the trace form.
  - The swaps make the handles alike.
  - All-trivial handles lie on one unipotent line.
- **(b)** For odd p, the Heisenberg character is fixed by every move, at every genus.
  - The moves act symplectically on H₁ mod p, since they keep ∂.
  - The character lives on the centre, through the commutator form.
  - Stone–von Neumann gives conjugacy.
- **(c)** The extraspecial 2-group character is fixed only at g = 1, where it is Q₈.
  - The squares give a quadratic form q.
  - A transvection T_u keeps q exactly when q(u) = 1.
  - The handle twists force q = 1 on the basis, and μ′ (μ made to keep ∂ exactly) is T_u with q(u) = 0.

**The checks (one run; every check as expected).**

| check | expected | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | the explicit moves keep ∂ exactly at g = 2, 3; the inverses compose to the identity; μ′ mod 2 is T_{b₁+a₂}; the twists mod 2 are T_{a_k}, T_{b_k} | 95% | **held** — all of it, at both genera |
| C2 | step 2 of (a), exact: Y = ±I only | 97% | **held** — exactly ±I |
| C3 | step 4 of (a), exact: X ∝ N | 99% | **held** |
| C4 | (a) by numerical search at g = 2: every zero trivial; at g = 1 the zeros trivial or quaternion | 85% | **held** — g = 2: 59 zeros from 120 starts, all trivial; the other 61 ends at defect ≥ 0.198. g = 1: 59 zeros, 8 trivial and 51 quaternion |
| C5 | (b): an intertwiner for every explicit move, H(3) at g = 1, 2 and H(5) at g = 1; the character formula | 95% | **held** — smallest singular values ≈ 10⁻¹⁶, the next ≈ √3 for H(3); the intertwiners unitary up to scale; 0 formula failures |
| C6 | (c): the transvection lemma at g = 1, 2, 3; one form equal to 1 off zero at g = 1, none at g = 2, 3; at g = 2 none of the sixteen forms kept by every move | 95% | **held** — the lemma without failure; Arf-1 counts 1, 6, 28; at g = 2 the twists keep only 1111, μ′ keeps exactly the eight forms with q(b₁ + a₂) = 1, and no form is kept by every move |

**What it shows.**
- **On the surface route, in SL(2, ℂ), the count is one handle: two records.** It is reached by the rank-two target,
  not by the democratic extension, which W109 and W110 used.
- **The prime is what decides it.** In the Heisenberg family the odd primes keep a fixed point at every genus. Only
  p = 2 is confined to one handle. Main's §3 argument is proved: on this route it is p = 2, not the extension, that
  gives two records.
- **The two routes compared.**
  - Under democracy the count of two holds on words with no target (W110) and on characters in SL(2, ℂ) (W109).
  - Under the surface's moves it holds on characters in SL(2, ℂ) (this arc), but not on words, since the boundary
    word is kept at every genus.
  - **Either way two records is characterised, not derived** (relay §168). What remains chosen is named: the target's
    rank (here SL(2), which fixes p = 2) on the surface route, and the extension on the democratic route.
- **Scope: orientation.** The moves keep ∂'s class, so they keep orientation. A move that reverses it sends ∂ to a
  conjugate of ∂⁻¹ and inverts the central character, so the odd-p character is then not fixed. p = 2 is unaffected.
  The web seat's hostile read of main's argument (14dfd318b, read after this arc's run) makes this point. It is
  consistent with (b) as stated. Taking such a move is GENESIS GM5c's swap question, which stays open.
- **Prior art.** Elementary, and probably known in some form. This seat has not searched the literature; main's ask
  to the referee lane covers it.

**Status.** PROVED (by hand; the proof committed before its checks; six checks, one recorded run, every one as
expected; two launches that wrote nothing, disclosed). A WEAVE result about the forms: every mapping class and every
character of the stated kinds, at every genus. 0 of 19.

## W110. The word side of the record count, by hand: for n ≥ 3 no non-trivial conjugacy class of F_n keeps even its length under every transvection, so none is kept; at n = 2 the kept classes are the powers of [a, b] (`W110_PROOF.md`; checks `the_kept_words.py`)

**Why.** Main's relay of 2026-10-20 (two records derived, §2) asks this seat for the word-side cell C4 from its relay
§162: "Count the conjugacy classes kept by every move at n = 3, 4. … That would join GM1 to PF1 on words" (GENESIS GM1,
the two records, and PF1). W109 settled the character side for every n.

**The order.**
- The proof (`W110_PROOF.md`) was worked by hand and committed first (6ed2c3373), with the four checks, their expected
  outcomes and priors.
- The checks script was committed before its one run (69313b426), and its output before it was read (a7f3878bb).

**Disclosed.**
- The pre-run review was by reading only; the script was byte-compiled, and nothing else was exercised before the run.
- Before the proof, only §162's exploratory note was on record.

**The theorem (PROVED).** R_ij is a_i ↦ a_i a_j and L_ij is a_i ↦ a_j a_i (i ≠ j); ‖v‖ is cyclic length.
- **(i) Every n ≥ 3.** If ‖R_ij^{±1}(w)‖ = ‖w‖ for every ordered pair, then w = 1. So no non-trivial class is kept by
  every R_ij, even up to inversion, and the same holds for the L_ij.
- **(ii) n = 2.** The classes kept by the record's R and L are exactly those of [a, b]^k. With the inversions they are
  kept only up to inversion.

**The proof of (i) in four lines** (in full in `W110_PROOF.md`).
1. **Whitehead's count.** ‖R_ij(w)‖ = m + n_i − 2c_ij, where c_ij counts the adjacent pairs a_i a_j⁻¹ and a_j a_i⁻¹.
   For R_ij⁻¹, c′_ij counts a_i a_j and a_j⁻¹ a_i⁻¹.
2. **Kept lengths.** If the lengths are kept, then c_ij = c′_ij = n_i/2. So every other letter a_j takes all n_i of
   a_i's right contacts: the successor of each a_i and the predecessor of each a_i⁻¹.
3. **The count.** n − 1 letters cannot each take all n_i contacts. So (n − 2)·n_i ≤ 0, and n_i = 0 for n ≥ 3.
4. **The left moves.** L_ij = rev ∘ R_ij ∘ rev, with rev the reversal of words.

**The checks (one run; every check as expected).**

| check | expected | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | the lemma by direct reduction, for every R_ij^{±1} and L_ij^{±1} on every class of the census | 95% | **held** — 0 failures on 34,998, 31,795 and 70,746 classes (n = 2, 3, 4); L_ij = rev R_ij rev on all |
| C2 | n = 3 to length 8, n = 4 to length 7: no class kept by the transvections or the full moves, exactly or up to inversion; none keeping its length | 97% | **held** — 0 in all ten counts |
| C3 | n = 2 to length 12: [a, b]^k for k = 1, 2, 3 in every count, except 0 for the full moves kept exactly | 95% | **held** — the three classes under ⟨L, R⟩, the transvections and the full moves up to inversion; 0 for the full moves exactly |
| C4 | the singular points of κ = −2 | 99% | **held** — only (0, 0, 0) |

- **Reported.** At n = 2, 178 classes keep their lengths under every R_ij^{±1}, and only the three powers are kept. The
  length condition decides n ≥ 3 by itself; at n = 2 it is necessary, not sufficient.

**What it shows.**
- **On words, as on characters, a non-trivial kept object exists only at two records.** At n ≥ 3 no class is kept, at
  any length, by any move set containing the transvections. The census's zeros are instances of a count, not a search
  bound.
- **At two records the kept word is the commutator.** Its trace is GENESIS PF1's κ = tr[a, b]. So the existence of a
  kept object joins GM1 (two records) to PF1 (the commutator) on words, as main asked.
  - **Corrected 2026-10-21** (main's S152, B1682; the web seat's read, 468aacd83). Three points.
    - **An equivalence.** The existence of a kept class is equivalent to two records, so it characterises GENESIS
      GM1; it is not a weaker input.
    - **Circular through κ.** Joined through κ, the link to PF1 is circular, since PF1's formal face is written for
      the two letters. What (i) and (ii) show without circularity is a statement about the moves: they keep the
      commutator class at n = 2 and nothing at n ≥ 3. A join to PF1 needs PF1's rank-free reading.
    - **The democratic extension.** (i) is about every a_i ↦ a_i a_j. A surface's own moves keep the boundary word
      at every genus, so on words the count of two rests on democracy.
    - The text above is kept as written.
- **A reading, not claimed new.** The kept character (W109's quaternion point) is the one singular point of the level
  surface κ = −2, which is the root's value of κ. On words the moves keep the commutator; on characters they keep the
  singular point of its root level.
- **Prior art.** Statement (i) is elementary, and probably known in some form; this seat has not searched the
  literature. (ii)'s converse is the cited mapping-class fact, checked to length 12.

**Status.** PROVED (by hand; the proof committed before its checks; four checks, one run, every one as expected). A
WEAVE result about the forms: every move and every conjugacy class, for all n ≥ 3 at once. 0 of 19.

## W109. B1677 for every n ≥ 3, by hand: the only character of F_n in SL(2, ℂ) fixed by every transvection is the trivial one, so a non-trivial common point exists only at two records, and the class reading follows for every finite subgroup of SU(2) (`W109_PROOF.md`; checks `the_record_count_for_every_n.py`)

**Why.** Main's relay of 2026-10-20 (the common point and the lifted register, §2) asks this seat for "a proof of B1677
for every n ≥ 3, or a counterexample at n ≥ 5". B1677's census stops at n = 4, because a sub-tuple can pass its filter
without generating.

**The order.**
- The proof (`W109_PROOF.md`) was worked by hand and committed first (2d10142d3), with the five checks, their expected
  outcomes and priors.
- The checks script was committed before its one run (6c395c4f7), and its output before it was read (7f12776ca).

**Disclosed.**
- The pre-run review was by reading only; the script was byte-compiled, and nothing else was exercised before the run.
- The proof does not rest on the checks.

**The theorem (PROVED).** F_n is free on a₁, …, a_n; R_ij is a_i ↦ a_i a_j and L_ij is a_i ↦ a_j a_i (i ≠ j).
- **(i) Every n ≥ 3.** A character of F_n in SL(2, ℂ) fixed by every R_ij is the trivial one. The same holds for the
  L_ij, or for one of the two per ordered pair.
- **(ii) n = 2.** The characters fixed by the record's R and L are exactly (2, 2, 2) and the quaternion point
  (0, 0, 0), and Aut(F₂) fixes both.
- **(iii) The class reading.** For n ≥ 3 and a non-trivial finite subgroup G of SU(2), no class of
  Epi(F_n, G)/Aut(G) is fixed by every R_ij.

**The proof in five lines** (in full in `W109_PROOF.md`). Let i, j and k be distinct; let t be the common trace.
1. The test word a_i gives tr(g_i g_j) = tr g_i. So every generator and every product of two has one trace, t.
2. The test word a_i a_j⁻¹ gives tr(g_i g_j⁻¹) = t. Fricke's identity then gives 2t = t², so t is 0 or 2.
3. The test word a_i a_k gives tr(g_i g_j g_k) = t.
4. At t = 0 the g_i are orthonormal for the trace form on sl(2, ℂ). Then g₁g₂ = ±g₃, and tr(g₁g₂g₃) = ∓2 ≠ 0.
5. At t = 2 every trace of at most three distinct generators is 2. By Horowitz and Procesi, the character is trivial.
- **For (iii).** R_ij⁻¹ = R_ik⁻¹ R_kj⁻¹ R_ik R_kj, so the automorphisms of G that the moves induce generate a perfect
  subgroup of Out(G). Out(G) is solvable for every finite subgroup of SU(2), so they are inner, and (i) applies.

**The checks (one run; every check as expected).**

| check | expected | prior | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Fricke's identity, its triple form, Cayley–Hamilton at trace 0, the polarisation, exact | 99% | **held** — every residual 0 |
| C2 | R_ij⁻¹ = R_ik⁻¹ R_kj⁻¹ R_ik R_kj, and the same for the L_ij, on F₃ and F₄ | 90% | **held** — 6 and 24 ordered triples, no failure |
| C3 | n = 2: the fixed characters of R and L are (0, 0, 0) and (2, 2, 2), both fixed by the inversion and the swap | 99% | **held** — and the reducer's R and L equal the hand formulas |
| C4 | n = 3, independent of the test words: the only fixed point on the character variety is (2, …, 2), for the six R_ij, the six L_ij and all twelve | 90% | **held** — each Groebner basis is exactly x_i − 2, y_ij − 2, z − 2; the reducer agrees with 2,400 random words to 8 × 10⁻¹⁵; the two t = 0 frames lie on the variety and are moved |
| C5 | Out(G) solvable for Q₈, 2T, 2O, 2I and Dic_m (3 ≤ m ≤ 12); \|Aut\| = 24, 24, 48, 120 and 2m·φ(2m); \|Inn\| = 4, 12, 24, 60 and 2m | 85% | **held** — Out(Q₈) = S₃ (solvable, not abelian); every other Out abelian, of order 2 for 2T, 2O and 2I |

**What it shows.**
- **B1677 holds for every n ≥ 3, with less input.**
  - Neither SU(2) nor a finite image is needed. Among all characters of F_n in SL(2, ℂ), a non-trivial one fixed by
    every move exists only at n = 2, and it is the quaternion point.
  - At n = 2 the finite image is forced: tr[a, b] = −2 there, so the point is irreducible, and it is Q₈'s
    representation up to conjugacy.
- **So the input behind two records (GENESIS GM1) shrinks.** It becomes: the records share a non-trivial point, fixed
  by every move, in SL(2, ℂ). The rank-two target stays priced. Whether the principle requires a common point stays a
  reading, as B1677 says.
  - **Corrected 2026-10-21** (main's S152, B1682; the web seat's read, 468aacd83). What shrinks is the hypothesis of
    the theorem: SU(2) and the finite image are not needed. The input behind two records does not shrink. For n ≥ 2 a
    non-trivial common character exists exactly when n = 2, so the input is equivalent to GENESIS GM1: a
    characterisation, not a derivation from something weaker. The selection rests on two named choices:
    - persistence, read as fixed up to conjugation;
    - the democratic extension of the moves, every a_i ↦ a_i a_j.
    - The text above is kept as written.
- **The census's work is one identity.** B1677's filter left the common trace t free. The test word a_i a_j⁻¹, with
  Fricke's identity, leaves only t = 0 and t = 2.
  - t = 0 is B1677's own rank-3 argument, made uniform in n.
  - t = 2 is the trivial character.
  - So n ≥ 5 needs nothing more, and no counterexample exists.
- **The class reading needs no census either** (§162's class-or-character question). For every n ≥ 3 and every finite
  subgroup of SU(2), the Galois twists of 2O, 2I and Dic_m included, the class reading gives the same answer as the
  character reading.
  - The mechanism is not transitivity. It is that the transvections generate a perfect group, while Out(G) is
    solvable.
  - W108's transitivity for 2I at n = 3 is a stronger, separate fact.
- **Prior art.** The statement is elementary and probably known. This seat has not searched the literature; main's
  ask to the referee lane covers it.

**Status.** PROVED (by hand; the proof committed before its checks; five checks, one run, every one as expected). A
WEAVE result about the forms: every move of the weave of n records and every character, for all n ≥ 3 at once. 0 of
19.

## W108. The binary icosahedral case of the record count, blind: at three records 2I has no common point, and the moves are transitive on all 13,344 classes of generating triples (`the_icosahedral_common_point.py`; `W108_RULE.md`)

**Why.** Main's foundations quest opens with P-205: does a weave of n records have an SU(2) common point only at
n = 2? Main's design is THE_COMMON_POINT_AND_THE_RECORD_COUNT_DESIGN.md.

**What it shows.**

- **R1, reported.**

  for the algebra, and the instrument measured the span. The failure is recorded as the instrument's, and the

  the joint action, and the weave fixes no number here, as B1633 found for the averaged word coupling.
